text: A genome-wide analysis identified 33 AsEPF/EPFL genes in oats (Avena sativa). Among these, 28 genes contain the conserved EPF domain and 5 genes harbor the stomagen domain.
Lutein, zeaxanthin, and beta-carotene were the major carotenoids. Several QTL were detected for each compound, color, and total carotenoids.

A half-sib population HZ595 (Hurdal x Z615-4, with 91 lines) was phenotyped in 2011 to validate QTL found in HZ595. Qdon.umb-17A/7C was localized with a phenotypic effect of 12.4%. Three SNPs linked to Qdon.umb-17A/7C were identified in both populations. One SNP each for QTL on 5C, 11A and 13A were identified in HZ595.

Three primers were designed from the identified SNP to develop an ASM for dehydration tolerance. The ASM produced a 261 bp fragment in all tolerant accessions and no amplification in sensitive accessions.

Nine QTL were identified for PCERGOT. Five QTL were identified using the overall data set. Four QTL were specific to the group data sets defined by temperature and humidity. QTL on SBI-02 and SBI-06 were validated in additional populations.
A GWAS involved 446 elite oat (Avena sativa L.) breeding lines from North America. They were genotyped with 1005 DArT markers and had phenotypic data from historical and balanced 2-year data.

This review integrates findings on the responses of S. viridis and S. italica to drought, heat, light, saline soils, nutrient deficiencies and heavy metal contamination. Comparative analyses highlight conserved and divergent stress-response pathways between S. italica and S. viridis.

One hundred and fourteen oat (Avena sativa L.) varieties were evaluated for genetic diversity using 77 molecular polymorphisms from eight AFLP primer combinations. Genetic similarity was calculated with the DICE coefficient for cluster analysis and principal component analysis.

qRT-PCR analysis showed that AtOAT transformation up-regulated the expression of proline biosynthesis genes TaOAT, TaP5CS, and TaP5CR, and down-regulated the proline catabolism gene TaP5CDH in transgenic plants under stress. Genes in the ornithine pathway (Orn-OAT-P5C/GSA-P5CR-Pro) were up-regulated, along with genes in the glutamate pathway (Glu-P5CS-P5C/GSA-P5CR-Pro).
AsSnRK2D, a member of the SnRK2 family, was isolated from oat (Avena sativa). The AsSnRK2D protein contains SnRK2 family-specific functional domains.

SNP markers for PcKM were tested on these populations and linkage maps were generated. Seventeen newly developed SNP markers from GBS data were mapped in these two populations and three other populations segregating for Pc45 or PcKM.
ABA treatment depressed most FtRCARs transcripts. ABA upregulated CHS, CHI, F3'H, F3H and FLS transcripts, while 4CL and PAL transcripts were down-regulated.

The proline content decreased in seeds with 4% and 16% moisture content, and increased in seeds with 28% moisture content. Proline played the main role in adaptation to oxidative stress in seeds with 28% moisture content. Antioxidant enzymes played the main role in seeds with 4% and 16% moisture content.

Six QTLs, qTB6, qSFW9, qJW9, qBrix2, qBrix10 and qSTI-Brix9, were main effect QTLs controlling salt tolerance with PVE > 10%. qSFW9 and qJW9 colocalized in marker interval SB5069-UGSM18 with PVEs of 17.70% and 14.20%, respectively, and positive effects from L-Tian. QTL clusters controlling PH, TB, STI-TB, SFW and JW were mapped in marker interval Xcup19-SB4177 on chromosome 7.

Gene co-expression networks constructed by WGCNA show distinct expression patterns of SbPLC1, SbPLC3a, and SbPLC4 under abiotic stress. qRT-PCR reveals expression level variations among most SbPLCs under drought, NaCl, NaHCO3, ABA treatments, and developmental stages, indicating specific and overlapping patterns. This analysis provides insights into SbPLCs roles in sorghum, their expression patterns, regulatory elements, and protein interactions under environmental stimuli and developmental stages.

Functional genomics techniques have enabled the identification of key genes implicated in defense responses against fungal pathogens in sorghum. Genome editing of identified resistance genes holds promise for developing high-performing varieties.

Lines or germplasm with the Seita.5G1346005UTR277+ allele exhibited significantly wider leaves than those with the Seita.5G1346005UTR277- allele, both within the RIL population and natural populations.

It reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation and increased chlorophyll content in sorghum leaves. Silencing SbMYC2 by virus-induced gene silencing compromised drought tolerance in sorghum seedlings.

Heritability for P-R and E-G was larger than for CGR, grain number per square meter, or yield. A multitrait, multienvironment analysis identified 12 QTL (LOD >= 2.5) for CGR, P-R, and E-G, explaining 21 to 36% of trait variability.
The lamina joint bending assay investigated if mutation of the rice homolog of SiCST1 affected brassinolide signaling. oscst1 exhibited insensitivity to exogenous BR treatment.

Among these QTNs and adjacent genes, 39 QTNs were repeatedly detected. 10 candidate genes were identified. 19 QTNs and two genes (sdw1/denso and Vrs1) were previously reported. 8 candidate genes need further validation.

Two oat cultivars with varied salt tolerance levels were used for metabolomic and transcriptomic characterization of adaptive responses to salt stress. Metabolomic profiling revealed 201 metabolites, including saccharides, amino acids, organic acids, and secondary metabolites.

Landraces possessed greater genetic diversity and contained most HvVRN1 alleles compared to modern commercial barley, especially in winter barley regions. HvVRN1 allele number diversity reduced significantly with higher growing latitudes, but increased in accessions carrying the winter HvVRN2 allele.

Drought affects sorghum growth and development. It impedes germination and embryonic structures through osmotic potential, reduces photosynthetic rates, and causes source-sink imbalance affecting seed filling. This reduces grain yield and quality. Sorghum responds to drought with morphological, physiological, and molecular alterations.

Comparative transcriptome profiling revealed differentially expressed transcripts associated with salt stress in pearl millet at 1, 3, and 7 hours of salt treatment. Salt stress increased proline, malondialdehyde, and hydrogen peroxide content in pearl millet at these time points. Pearl millet regulated superoxide dismutase, catalase, and peroxidase activities to reduce salinity impact.

An analysis of candidate genes associated with six significant markers revealed immune receptors and putative disease resistance proteins. This genomic region on chromosome 4A is associated with crown rust resistance in oats.
TaTPP-7A is expressed in developing grains and influences grain filling and size. Overexpression of TaTPP-7A in wheat enhances grain TKW and yield.

Representative single plant selections (SPS) from the two sub-populations were grown with SPS from off-type plants and plants from the original AV25 composite mixture. Plants were genotyped by DNA extraction of 96 samples. SNPs were detected using an Illumina Infinium 6K Chip assay.

Seventy-six QTLs were mapped using recombinant inbred lines (RIL) population Arta x Harmal-2//Esp/1808-4L, evaluated in dry and semi-dry areas over 3 years. Traits included grain yield, biological yield, harvest index, kernel weight, seed per head, days to heading, kernel filling duration, growth vigour, growth habit, lodging and plant height.

The study built global and seed-preferential co-expression networks of starch synthesis pathways. These networks indicated that photosynthesis and microtubule-based movement play important roles in starch synthesis. The study generated a global transcriptome atlas of sorghum. This atlas provides a functional genomics resource for trait discovery and insight into starch synthesis regulation in sorghum.

Single marker analysis associated 29 markers with plant response to greenbug feeding damage. Interval mapping, composite interval mapping and multiple interval mapping identified four major QTLs for greenbug resistance on chromosome 9.

text: This study investigated three foxtail millet cultivars with different drought resistance. Exploring candidate genes for foxtail millet drought resistance and revealing its molecular regulatory mechanism and metabolic pathway is significant.
SbPUB genes are unevenly distributed on the 10 chromosomes of sorghum. Most SbPUB genes (16) are on chromosome 4. No SbPUB genes are on chromosome 5.

Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) is a crop with salt and drought tolerance. 16 PLATZ genes are identified in foxtail millet. These genes are mainly expressed in roots and panicles and are induced by abiotic stresses.

Tan1 and Tan2 play a major role in seed dormancy and induce resistance against soil-borne pathogens under cold and wet soil conditions. Seed tannin content may be used as an indirect selection marker for identifying cold tolerant germplasm for breeding.

Pm3 is the only powdery mildew resistance gene previously mapped on Mrg18. However, the pm3 differential line Mostyn was susceptible to the powdery mildew race used in this study, indicating that Pm3 and QPm.18 are different genes.

A genome-wide association study identified 36 significant QTNs associated with three Striga resistance indices. In sorghum, 33 potential candidate genes are located near 17 strongly associated and reliable QTNs.

The rutin content (RC) of 101 natural TB materials ranged from 14.08 to 24.50 mg/g, with an average of 19.46 mg/g. This revealed substantial natural variation in RC. Furthermore, 314,166 high-quality SNPs were identified through whole-genome resequencing.
Oat cultivars were subjected to drought stress from plant growth to the two-leaf stage using a pot-based water withholding method. Stress durations were 0 d, 7 d, and 14 d.

Marker-assisted backcrossing (MABC) pyramided a CLS resistance gene and two PM resistance genes from donor parent D2 into susceptible variety KING. Five markers linked to the resistance genes were used for foreground selection. Two marker sets [Set A with 15 polymorphic SSR and EST-SSR markers, Set B with 34 polymorphic ISSR loci] were used for background selection.

A global collection of Fagopyrum esculentum and Fagopyrum tataricum (190 and 51 accessions) was characterized using 37 agro-morphological traits and 24 SSR markers. Variation was observed for most traits.

The study investigated five major Shanxi Province cultivars of foxtail millet (Setaria italica) released from the 1970s to 2020s. It assessed yield, agronomic traits, photosynthesis, photosynthetic products, and canopy structure under field conditions.

Genes related to physiological traits are involved in starch and sucrose metabolism, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, glutathione metabolism, and plant hormone signal transduction. The active oxygen metabolism system and soluble protein of proso millet root are regulated by protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity.

The autopolyploid showed few gene expression changes over long periods and under drought stress. However, more DEGs and up-regulated DEGs were observed between autotetraploid and diploid than in the CK. Genome duplication also resulted in gain or loss of drought-related genes, which may help autopolyploid survive better under drought.

Cool temperatures limit sorghum growth in temperate areas. Some Chinese landraces show higher emergence and greater seedling vigor under cool conditions than most breeding lines, but lack desirable agronomic characteristics.

The study aimed to identify genomic regions and candidate genes for drought tolerance traits to guide marker-assisted breeding. Ninety-nine groundnut genotypes were phenotyped under drought-stressed and non-stressed field conditions in 2018/19 and 2019/20, and using the LeasyScan platform under non-stressed conditions in 2019/20 at ICRISAT/India.

Crown rust resistance is described in oat diploid species A. strigosa accession PI 258731. Resistance from PI 258731 is introgressed into hexaploid A. sativa germplasm. This study maps QTL for resistance in PI 258731. It evaluates the number of QTL. It understands the relationship between the genomic location in A. strigosa and the introgression location in A. sativa. It identifies molecular markers linked with PI 258731 resistance loci. These markers could be used for marker assisted selection and detection of this resistance in diverse A. strigosa accessions.

34 main-effect QTLs were identified for traits: heading date, plant height, lodging, visual score, grain yield, kernel weight, milling yield, test weight, thin and plump kernels, groat beta-glucan concentration, oil concentration, and protein. Several QTLs correspond to those in homologous or homoeologous regions reported in other oat studies.

Allelic variation in 'QTL-hotspot' improves pre-anthesis water use, transpiration efficiency, root architecture and canopy development, enabling high-yield performance under terminal drought. CaTIFY4b may regulate organ size under water deficit by modulating GIF1 expression.

The proso millet cultivar 'Yumi 2' was analyzed under stimulated drought stress using 20% PEG-6000. SOD activity, POD activity, soluble protein content, MDA, and O-2(-) content increased with drought stress time but decreased after rehydration.
EBR application up-regulated CqBIN2 transcript levels and proline biosynthesis genes. Silencing CqBIN2 by VIGS reduced drought tolerance, survival rate, and proline content in quinoa seedlings.

Genomic regions contributing to genetic differentiation suggest loci related to growth habit and stress resistance were under intense selection, not hulless-related regions. Genome-wide association analysis detected four markers highly associated with hullessness.

We identified candidate genes for salt tolerance in quinoa. Some DEGs were exclusively expressed in the ST genotype. DEGs common to both genotypes under salt stress may be key genes for quinoa salinity adaptation.

Genic SSR markers were developed from mungbean transcriptome sequences and transferred to related Vigna species. EST sequences from mungbean genotype 'Jangan' were searched for SSRs. 2,299 SSR motifs from 1,848 SSR-containing unique ESTs were identified.
Foxtail millet grain is rich in nutrition. Foxtail millet is tolerant to abiotic stresses including drought.

Expression profiling of NILs and qRT-PCR assays showed changes in predicted genes at 30 and 45 DAF in leaf tissues of qSTG introgressed lines. There was a significant difference in transcript levels of genes between different DAF. QTL pyramiding has potential for improving plant performance under adverse environmental conditions.

The sterile lines 521A and 170A, and the restorer lines Ji318R and 0-30 were promising parents with high general combining ability. All endogenous substances of root bleeding sap were positively correlated with the sum of parental general combining ability at highly significant levels. IAA, CTK, GA3, ABA, soluble sugar, amino acid, and root bleeding intensity were positively correlated with male general combining ability at significant or highly significant levels.

An in silico B.Tx623 wx(a) genome assembly was constructed from the B.Tx623 reference genome (v3.1.1) to include the insertion, a similar to 5-kb-long terminal repeat (LTR) copia retrotransposon. This in silico wxa assembly improved read mapping at Sobic.010G022600 in wx(a) individuals, identified 78 new uniquely mapped reads, and enabled distinguishing different Waxy genotypes using short-read sequencing data.

Transcriptome profiling from 1 to 25 dpa reveals dynamic gene expression pathways. These pathways shift from cellular growth and embryo development (1–5 dpa) to cell division, fatty acid biosynthesis (5–25 dpa), and seed storage compounds synthesis in the endosperm (5–25 dpa). Network analysis identifies 361 hub genes linked to starch synthesis in the endosperm and 207 hub genes linked to protein synthesis in the endosperm. This will help breeders enhance sorghum grain quality.

4552 and 4845 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified in XCq and QCq under cold stress, respectively. KEGG pathway analysis showed the MAPK signaling pathway was only among up-regulated DEGs in XCq. The expression of DEGs encoding transcription factors AP2/ERF, bHLH, bZIP, MYB, ICEs, and CORs related to cold response was higher in XCq than in QCq under cold stress.

Transcriptome analysis identified 588 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 383 up-regulated and 205 down-regulated. The DEGs were associated with ribosomes, plant hormone signal transduction, and photosynthesis. Additionally, 549 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified in maize leaves under both monocropping and maize-peanut intercropping systems.

QTLs for height of the tallest basal tiller, number of basal tillers per plant, panicle length, leaf angle, maturity, and awn length were mapped. Three or more QTLs were mapped in linkage groups A, E, G, and I. No QTLs were mapped in linkage groups B and D.

Transcriptomic data identified seven differentially expressed AsaPP2C genes: Asa_chr6Dg00217, Asa_chr6Ag01950, Asa_chr3Ag01998, Asa_chr5Ag00079, Asa_chr4Cg03270, Asa_chr6Cg02197, and Asa_chr7Dg02992, validated via qRT-PCR.

DPY1 is phosphorylated and activated in response to osmotic stress. DPY1 is required for osmotic stress-induced phosphorylation events, including phosphorylation of SnRK2s. DPY1 acts upstream of SAPK6 and is required for full SAPK6 activation, regulating downstream genes in response to drought stress.
Pearl millet is tolerant to heat and drought. It can be used to identify heat-resistant genes.

LN improved the expression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes. The transcriptional regulation mediated by MYB and bHLH was analyzed. 78 transcription factors, 124 small secreted peptides and 38 receptor-like protein kinases encoding genes were involved in LN response.

A population of 184 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) was derived from the cross E36-1 x SPV570. The RILs and parents were phenotyped for yield component traits in field and root traits in an above ground rhizotron. High heritability and genetic advance were estimated for all root traits and most yield traits.

In class U, CqGSTU22, CqGSTU67, CqGSTU43, CqGSTU42, and CqGSTU15 were strongly expressed in various tissues and organs. In class L, CqGSTL1 and CqGSTL5 were strongly expressed. In class Z, CqGSTZ5 was strongly expressed. In DHAR class, CqDHAR2 and CqDHAR3 were strongly expressed. CqGSTU66, CqGSTF20, and CqGSTF23 were not expressed in the tested tissues or organs.

FtMYB13, a R2R3-MYB from Tartary buckwheat, is located in the nucleus and is not a transcriptional activator. Compared to wild type (WT), transgenic Arabidopsis overexpressing FtMYB13 showed lower ABA sensitivity and improved drought/salt tolerance. This was due to higher proline content, greater photosynthetic efficiency, higher transcript abundance of stress-related genes, and smaller amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA).

Drought tolerance of mung bean cultivars/lines was examined based on seed germination characteristics, antioxidative potential, and nutrient uptake. PEG-induced drought adversely affected germination enzyme activities, seed germination attributes, seedling biomass production, and nutrient uptake. Total soluble proteins (TSP) and malondialdehyde (MDA) contents increased.

The genes are distributed across seven chromosomes and classified into ten subfamilies. The encoded proteins vary in length, physicochemical properties, and predicted subcellular localization, with most members containing the conserved PP2Cc catalytic domain.

QJy-sbi06 was located in a 21.2 kb region on chromosome 6. The candidate gene sobic.006G147400, encoding an NAC transcription factor, was identified in this region. Association analysis and sequencing showed that XL52 has a 1.8 kb transposon insertion in the NAC gene, which interrupts and inactivates the juice yield gene.
300 quinoa accessions were screened for adaptation to low-altitude areas using seventeen traits. The experiment was conducted in Taigu District, Shanxi Province in 2021.
Marker Xtxp211 significantly affected seedling vigor and emergence in both populations. Loci interactions were also significant.

Candidate genes are associated with QTL for insect resistance. The study genetically mapped the candidate genes and identified their association with shoot fly resistance. It updated the genetic map with new markers to locate additional QTL.

Water deficit stress affects mung bean growth and reduces yield. A field experiment evaluated four water stress-tolerant genotypes: BARI Mung-8, BMX-08010-2, BMX-010015, and BMX-08009-7, along with two check varieties, BARI Mung-6 and BARI Mung-7, across five environments.

It has a short life cycle, high harvest index, low planting costs, strong adaptability and resistance. This study reveals sodium ion (Na+) toxicity resistance strategies from germination to seedling stage, root to leaf, and phenotype to mechanism.

A genome-wide analysis of foxtail millet identified 93 MAPK cascade genes: 15 SiMAPKs, 10 SiMAPKKs, and 68 SiMAPKKKs. These genes are distributed on nine chromosomes of foxtail millet. Phylogenetic analysis divided SiMAPKs and SiMAPKKs into four subgroups each, and SiMAPKKKs into three subgroups: Raf, ZIK, and MEKK.
114 CqGST genes were identified from the quinoa genome. The phylogenetic tree showed these genes divided into seven subgroups.

Haplotype analysis linked three SbPaO genes to thousand-grain weight (TGW). Superior haplotypes SbPaO1-hap4, SbPaO3-hap5, and SbPaO4-hap4 increased TGW. Single-gene improvements increased TGW by 10.57-17.20%, dual-gene aggregation by 18.78-24.75%, and three-gene aggregation by 29.09%.

RT-qPCR characterized AsNAC gene expression in different tissues and its response to abiotic stresses. Collinearity analysis identified segmental duplication as the main driver of oat NAC gene family expansion. The functions of AsNAC109 in regulating abiotic stress tolerance were clarified in Arabidopsis.
In the XiNong 9943 genotype, SOD, POD, CAT, and APX levels at 30% PEG were 2.01, 2.19, 4.92, and 4.46 times higher, respectively, than under normal growth condition (T0).

Understanding the genetic and molecular factors regulating carbohydrate metabolism is necessary to improve legume starch content, quality, and quantity. This review assessed the genetic and molecular basis of legume carbohydrate components, focusing on seed starch content. It provided an overview of starch biosynthesis in heterotrophic organs, the chemical composition of major consumable legumes, factors influencing starch digestibility, and advances in genetic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic studies in important legume crops.

Three QTNs were associated with days to 50% flowering; two each with leaf-to-stem ratio and number of nodes per plant; and one each with plant height, leaf width, number of leaves per plant, stem girth, and internodal length. Six candidate genes were associated with days to 50% flowering, two each with leaf width, stem girth, leaf-to-stem ratio, and number of nodes per plant, and one each with plant height, number of leaves per plant, and internodal length. FarmCPU was the most suitable model for controlling false positives and false negatives. Analysis of the QTNs may identify new candidate genes for the trait.
HvASR2 and HvASR3 expression in barley seedlings was influenced by salt, osmotic, and ABA treatments. HvASR2 is a transcriptional repressor, and HvASR3 is a transcriptional activator.
Most CqAP2/ERF genes showed distinct expression patterns in different tissues and developmental stages. Five CqAP2/ERF genes responded to drought, high temperature, salt, and low phosphorus.

Map-based cloning showed an eight-base pair deletion in the sixth exon of wp1.a in LOC101786849, causing premature termination. WP1 encodes phytoene synthase.
High contribution QTLs were distributed on seven out of 11 linkage groups. Many small contribution QTLs were found.
Selected silicoDArT markers were used for chromosomal localization of resistance genes. Five of 71 segregating silicoDArT markers for the Pm11 gene were found on the oat consensus genetic map.

Gene editing generated three new haplotypes of the sdw1/denso candidate gene gibberellin 20-oxidase2 (GA20ox2). These haplotypes induced a dwarfing phenotype, enhanced yield potential, and promoted seed dormancy to reduce pre-harvest sprouting. Beta-amylase activity in the grains of the mutant lines was significantly increased, which benefits malt quality.

Drought interactions with abiotic stresses and biotic factors can increase crop vulnerability or enhance drought tolerance. Modern plant breeding techniques can develop locally adapted, drought tolerant, and nutrient rich sorghum cultivars.

Kruskall-Wallis and multiple-QTL model mapping identified QTL associated with drought response phenotypes. The QTL were reproducible between stg and rdw under greenhouse conditions. Field studies confirmed all ten drought-response QTL observed under greenhouse conditions.

The expression levels of three SWEET genes and four PIP genes were higher in YG than in An. This allocated more photosynthetic sugar to the roots. The high expression levels of SiPIPs enhanced root water transport capacity.

We evaluated simulated traits from maize (Zea mays L.) and sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] diversity panels using ridge-regression best linear unbiased prediction (RR-BLUP) models. The models included fixed-effect covariates tagging peak GWAS signals. The covariates increased genomic selection (GS) prediction accuracy in the RR-BLUP model under various genetic architectures and genomic backgrounds.

Three major stable pleiotropic QTLs (qSCS-1, qRLS-1, and qLNN-1) were associated with SCR, RL, and RN in both normal and salinity treatments. Two major stable pleiotropic QTLs (qSNN-3 and qLWS-3) associated with SN and LW are promising for MAS. Two major-effect QTLs (SCot8-B-CAAT5-D and HVM54-Bmag0571) on chromosomes 1 and 2 were characterized for their positive allele effect, which can be used to develop barley varieties for drought conditions.
ABA Insensitive 5 (ABI5) is a basic leucine zipper transcription factor. There is minimal research on the ABI5 family in foxtail millet.
GsNAC2 overexpression upregulated key glutathione biosynthesis genes. It increased GR and GSH-Px activities and accumulated more GSH after saline-alkali treatment.

SNPs induced by EMS were unevenly distributed across all 18 chromosomes, with an average mutation frequency of 91.2 SNPs/Mb. A positive correlation between SNP number and chromosome length was identified.

Restriction site polymorphisms were used to investigate co-location of candidate genes with QTL for seedling drought stress-induced premature senescence in cowpea. Genomic DNA from 113 F-2:8 RILs of drought-tolerant IT93K503-1 and susceptible CB46 genotypes was digested with EcoR1, HpaII, Mse1, or Msp1 restriction enzymes and amplified with primers from 13 drought-responsive cDNAs.
Two minor QTLs (qBX3.1 and qBX7.1) for Brix (BX) were mapped on chromosomes 3 and 7. The QTLs in two clusters (qPH7.1/qBX7.1 and qPH7.1/qFBW7.1) overlapped for PH, FBW and BX.

A drought tolerance QTL on chromosome 2 was transferred from barley cultivar 'Tadmor' to cultivars 'Baronesse' and 'Aydanhanim'. The QTL's effects on drought tolerance and other traits were studied using near-isogenic lines in controlled environments and field trials.

Drought and HT tolerance can be improved by understanding tolerance mechanisms, screening germplasm to identify tolerant lines, and incorporating those traits into elite breeding lines. Systems approaches identify the best tolerance donors for SSA and SA sorghum breeding programs.

Hexaploid amphiploids have the AACCDD genome composition, while octoploid amphiploids have AACCCCDD, AAAACCDD, or AABBCCDD compositions. The A, B, C, and D oat genomes differ in involvement in non-centromeric, intercalary translocations.

Nineteen genes for anthocyanin biosynthesis were annotated in this genomic region. Gene Si1g06530 encodes a SANT/Myb domain protein and was highly expressed in developing panicles and seeds. It is a candidate gene for the brown hull color of Jigu 31.
SNP marker technologies and haplotype-based GWAS are applied methods for molecular breeding in barley. CRISPR-Cas9 technology uses genetic information for gene editing, as in the cv. Golden Promise.
The QTL QSc/Sl.cib-7H has strong effects on spike length (SL) and spike compactness (SC). This was validated in two pairs of near isogenic lines (NILs) and diverse genetic backgrounds.

Two genes, Seita.5G251300 and Seita.8G036300, exhibit drought-tolerant haplotypes. These haplotypes have an advantage in 1000 grain weight and main panicle grain weight, without penalty in grain weight per plant.

A major QTL with 13.75% contribution rate is located on barley chromosome 7H (GBM1303-GMS056). A minor QTL with 6.01% contribution rate is located on chromosome 2H (Scssr03381-Scssr07759). It comes from the high-value parent ZGMLEL.

The region has a strong association with growth habit, suggesting a pleiotropic effect on both traits. This provides a molecular explanation for the early flowering of domesticated chickpea and the growth habit locus Hg.

The study identified the ZF-HD family in quinoa and a drought-responsive CqZF-HD14 gene. Transient overexpression of CqZF-HD14 promotes photosynthetic pigment accumulation under drought stress, strengthens the antioxidant system, and enhances drought tolerance.

Principal component analysis transformed 21 conventional traits into seven independent indexes. Regression analysis selected these indicators: second leaf from the top surface area, peroxidase activity, catalase activity, malondialdehyde content, chlorophyll (a + b), grain weight per ear, and yield.

Transcriptome data before and after drought stress in foxtail millet hybrid Zhangza 19 and its parents identified 5597 DEGs. WGCNA screened 607 drought-tolerant genes. Heterotic genes were screened based on expression level.

Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) is a crop grown in semi-arid tropics where drought constrains productivity. To understand the genetic basis and identify QTL for drought tolerance, two RIL populations ICGS 76 x CSMG 84-1 (RIL-2) and ICGS 44 x ICGS 76 (RIL-3) were used.
VfAP2-1 and VfERF-99 enhance pathogen resistance. They positively influence ROS homeostasis, accumulating H2O2 and O2- under abiotic and biotic stresses, inhibiting pathogen colonization.

This study mapped QTLs for agronomic and yield traits using three connected mapping populations of different genetic backgrounds in Ethiopian sorghum germplasm. The three bi-parental populations, each with 207 F 2:3 lines, were evaluated under two moisture stress environments.

We performed QTL mapping of agronomic traits in a RIL population derived from a cross between Sorghum propinquum and Sorghum bicolor inbred Tx7000. Using low-coverage Illumina sequencing and bin-mapping, we generated ~1920 bin markers spanning ~875 cM.
SbWRKY50 directly binds to the upstream promoter of the SOS1 gene in A. thaliana. In sweet sorghum, SbWRKY50 directly binds to the upstream promoters of SOS1 and HKT1.
The crop has adaptation to drought, salinity, and high temperatures. It is susceptible to low temperatures.

This hypersensitivity was alleviated by elevated K+ levels, indicating SbHKT1;4 may mediate K+ uptake under excessive Na+. Electrophysiology in Xenopus laevis oocytes demonstrated SbHKT1;4 transports Na+ and K+.

Molecular diversity of 40 Tibetan wild barley accessions, 10 Syrian, 72 North American, 36 European, 9 South American, and 8 Australian varieties was characterized using multiple microsatellite loci. The 42 SSR primers amplified 278 alleles across the 175 barley accessions.
Three and two QTNs were detected by three and two multi-locus methods, respectively. One QTN on chromosome 5 is associated with CP, NDF, and ADF.
SiPLATZ12 overexpression increases Na+ accumulation, decreases K+ accumulation, and lowers vacuolar pH. SiPLATZ12 overexpression represses transcription of most NHX, SOS, and CBL genes.
Two QTL clusters contained overlapping QTLs for PH, FW and DW. Orthologs of three SD candidate genes from maize were found within two SD QTLs.
Sorghum dwarfing genes Dw1, Dw2, and Dw3 are crucial for plant architecture and yield. Their allelic distribution was analyzed in 241 Chinese landrace accessions.

SbWRKY51 ectopic expression in Arabidopsis showed similar phenotypes. Mutation of the homologous gene AtWRKY11 increased salt sensitivity in Arabidopsis. Under salt stress, SbWRKY51-overexpressed transgenic sorghum altered expression of oxidative stress and lignin biosynthesis genes and increased lignin content.

The strip-till fertilizer application depth was 13-15 cm below the soil surface. Corn planted 10 cm from the fertilized row showed greater early season growth, higher plant population, and higher grain yield.

Genes regulating chlorophyll content (CC) and relative water content (RWC) under abiotic stress were screened using WGCNA. Gene-trait correlations were defined as modules, each denoted by a color.
The locus explained 15% of phenotypic variance in GWAS and 64% in QTL mapping. Pm13 confers APR, confirmed by comparing field data with laboratory leaf segment tests.
The down-regulation of ribosomal protein-related genes causes stunted growth in salt-sensitive accessions. The salt-tolerant accession alleviates salt stress by increasing energy production.

Rice-Tartary is an easily-shelled local variety. The F-2 segregating population was constructed by crossing Yunqiao No.1 (hard-shelled) and Rice-Tartary (easily-shelled). BSA-seq was used for initial mapping.

Foliar resistance to Ascochyta lentis is controlled by a dominant gene (AbR(1)) in lentil accession ILL5588 ('Northfield'). Flanking RAPD markers linked to the resistance locus were identified by bulked segregant analysis.
The dendrogram from SSR molecular marker data grouped the genotypes into three clusters. The SSR marker data showed a narrow genetic base in mungbean genotypes.

The S. italica genome was sequenced in 2012, but lacked high-density genetic maps linked to agronomic and yield traits. We resequenced a foxtail millet population of 439 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) and developed a high-resolution bin map with high-density SNP markers for gene identification.

A pot experiment investigated the effect of foliar application of gibberellic acid, kinetin, and salicylic acid under salt stress on two sweet sorghum varieties, Yajin 13 and Yajin 71. Parameters included Na+, K+, Ca2+, P, and Mg2+ content, photosynthetic rate, transpiration rate, stomatal conductance, and membrane permeability.

Four novel QTL were identified. Qstna.sau-5H and Qnhi.sau-5H are N-related QTL unaffected by N treatment. Qtgw.sau-2H is for thousand-grain weight. Qph.sau-3H is for plant height. Qsl.sau-7H is for spike length. Qal.sau-7H is for awn length. These four QTL are stable expression QTL.
Fungal resistance genes are identified for breeding. Quantitative trait loci mapping studies have reported genomic regions linked to fungal disease resistance.
Sorghum is a genetically diversified grain crop grown in semiarid regions. Drought stress severely restricts its production and reduces its productivity and nutritional quality.

Beta-1,3-glucanase (XnhsbmSFC4/SBI-10) is involved in aphid and brown planthopper resistance. It was associated with deadhearts% and leaf glossiness. Comparative QTL analysis revealed common QTL for shoot fly, greenbug, head bug, and midge.

Genome-wide screening developed SSR markers associated with six major agronomic traits and rutin contents in 97 core germplasm resources. 40,901 SSR loci were identified; they were uniformly distributed throughout the TB genome, with a mean distance of 11 kb between loci.

The study maps genomic regions for terminal heat- and drought-stress tolerance in barley. A hundred lines from a ND24260 x Flagship doubled haploid population were evaluated for stay-green expression.

The research evaluated the purity and relationships of the original oats (Avena sativa L.) variety AV-25 and two multi-line sub-populations AV25-T and AV25-S. Both sub-populations are useful as forages in the central highland region of Colombia, which includes the departments of Boyaca and Cundinamarca. They were derived from the original composite mixture Avena 25, used in the mountainsides of the southern department of Narino.
Triploid Miscanthus × giganteus is a sterile perennial grass used for biomass production. A scale standardizing description of M. × giganteus morphological stages has not been developed.

The cDNA clone (GenBank accession no. GT090998) codes for a putative DREB2 protein. It was isolated as a differentially expressed gene from a 6 h dehydration stress SSH library.

The anthracnose resistance in sorghum line SC112-14 (Cs-SC112) was studied using F2 progenies and recombinant inbred lines against pathotypes from Puerto Rico, Texas, Arkansas, and Georgia. Haplotype combinations of these genes explain the segregation of the senescence trait in a recombinant inbred population.
Avena sativa has greater salt stress tolerance than Avena nuda. The cultivars' salt tolerance ranking is: 'Qinghai 444' > 'Mengyan No. 1' > 'Baiyan No. 18' > 'Qingyin No. 3'.

Sorghum is a model crop for abiotic stress research due to its small genome and tolerance to drought, salinity-alkalinity, and heat. Advances include gapless reference genomes, pan-genome analyses of structural variation, and population resequencing revealing domestication signatures and stress adaptation loci.

The study identified the SbMYBHv33 transcription factor, which is downregulated by salt, drought, and ABA in the salt-tolerant sorghum inbred line M-81E. Overexpression of SbMYBHv33 in sorghum significantly reduced biomass accumulation and salinity tolerance at the seedling stage.

STRUCTURE, phylogenetic, and PCoA analyses grouped most Ethiopian and Turkish broomcorn accessions together. Most East Asian accessions from China and South Korea formed another group. Two Sudanese broomcorn individuals were in a distinct group.

An F-6:8 RIL population from the cross between WAOAT2132 (Dw6) and Caracas, and the two parents, were used to evaluate the genetic effects of the Dw6 dwarfing gene on plant height and other agronomic traits in oat (Avena sativa L.) across three environments, and to develop closely linked markers for MAS for Dw6. The parents differed in all agronomic traits except whorl number.

Six genes from five subfamilies were characterized for expression responses to abiotic stresses. Overexpression of SiABI5.12 confers osmotic stress tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana, demonstrating SiABI5 function in abiotic stress response.

AP2/ERF genes in Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and barley are extensively studied. In quinoa, AP2/ERF genes lacked systematic investigation. This study identified and characterized AP2/ERF genes in quinoa genome-wide. 105 CqAP2/ERF genes were identified. Phylogenetic analysis classified them into 5 subfamilies.

Sixty-six genotypes were resistant to at least one of six races. Twenty-two genotypes were resistant to all six races. These 22 genotypes were resistant to bulk inoculum at the seeding stage and to natural populations of Pca at the adult plant stage.
105 M-QTLs with 3.48-33.36% PVE were identified using QTL Cartographer. 65 M-QTLs with 1.3-15.01% PVE were identified using QTLNetwork. 53 M-QTLs were identified using both programmes.

High water uptake varieties have loosely structured starch granules. Low water uptake varieties have compact starch granules. The compactness of starch granules may be associated with seed imbibition.

HN16 and its mutated line asm1 were studied. H2O2 was examined for its role in sorghum against aphid. Constitutive H2O2 was the main factor for increased aphid tolerance. Aphid feeding also induced increased H2O2 concentration. Studying ROS scavenging enzymes found APX and GPX were closely related. SOD, POX and CAT were not involved in RMES1-mediated resistance.

Genetic modeling revealed carotenoid content is controlled by three major-gene pairs plus polygenes (MX3-AI-A model). Major-gene heritability is 96.65% and polygene heritability is 3.35%. Three elite RILs with higher carotenoid and superior agronomic performance were identified for marker-assisted backcrossing.

Different natural growth environments resulted in adaptation, with significant differences in salt tolerance between northern and southern Chinese Tartary buckwheat populations. Using selective sweep scanning and a genome-wide association study, we identified genes responsible for Tartary buckwheat domestication and differentiation, which were experimentally validated.

Cis-acting elements ABRE, MYB, ARE, and STRE were identified in the promoters of HvASRs. The expression of HvASRs was influenced by salt, osmotic, and ABA treatments in barley seedling roots and leaves.

The salt tolerance-related genes are well studied in Arabidopsis and soybean, but limited in mungbean. We mined salt tolerance related genes using the survival rate trait and 160,1405 SNPs in 112 mungbean accessions. VrFRO8 significantly associated with salt-stress were identified in the GWAS analysis.

A comparative transcriptome analysis was performed on wild types, landraces, and improved cultivars of broomcorn millet at seeding and filling stages. The analysis identified genes selected during domestication and improvement. Variations in gene expression patterns between wild types and landraces, and between landraces and improved cultivars, were evaluated to explore molecular mechanisms of domestication and improvement.

Three genomic regions contained QTLs for seed weight and days to flowering, linking the traits. Comparing these QTLs with those in azuki bean [Vigna angularis] and rice bean [Vigna umbellata] showed conservation across the three Vigna species.

GWAS using SNP markers identified two genomic loci on chromosomes 2 and 9 associated with blast disease resistance in foxtail millet. Eight putative genes were identified using rice blast transcriptomic data.

The map length was 1,654 cM with an average marker interval of 16.4 cM. The 81 SSR markers were unevenly distributed across nine chromosomes. Chromosome 8 had the fewest markers (3) and chromosome 9 had the most (18). Sorghum has lower water requirements and compact growth in accessions like TX430 and BTx623, making it practical for genome editing studies. Maize shares close genetic similarity with Sorghum and belongs to the Panicoideae subfamily, so it could benefit from Sorghum-based insights.

Genotypes with the one-kbp insertion of the HvAACT1 gene had high mean performance for all measured traits. Lines without the insertion had the lowest mean value. Marker-assisted selection accelerates selection of acid-tolerant barley lines.

The C2 cluster contained QTL for yield, agronomic, and N-related traits. Among novel QTL, Qstna.sau-5H and Qnhi.sau-5H expression was unaffected by N treatment.

GWAS identified seven SNP markers. SNP2 and SNP3 positively correlated with beta-glucan. SNP1, SNP4, SNP5, SNP6, and SNP7 negatively correlated with beta-glucan. Candidate genes HORVU7Hr1G000320 and HORVU7Hr1G000040 are linked to SNP7 and belong to the nucleotide triphosphate hydrolase superfamily, which may affect beta-glucan synthase activity.

Four loci for flag leaf thickness (FLT) were detected in barley. The loci are located on chromosome arms 2H, 3H, 5H and 6H. They were identified by assessing 201 recombinant inbred lines in field and glasshouse trials across seasons.

Genome-wide association studies identify genetic loci linked to grain micronutrient traits, including high iron content. These resources support molecular breeding and marker-assisted selection to improve little millet.

GWAS detected 46 SNPs associated with traits. An SNP on chromosome 6 is linked to lysine with a phenotypic contribution of 49.62%. Candidate gene analysis identified 138 genes within 100 kb of significant QTLs. These genes are involved in metabolic and biosynthetic pathways including amino acid and carbohydrate metabolism.

Post-anthesis drought adversely impacted the growth, morphology, and biomass accumulation of Tartary buckwheat. Drought stress enhanced the maximum photosynthetic capacity (Fv/Fm) and light protection ability (NPQ) of the 'Xiqiao-2' genotype.

Cowpea is tolerant to drought and salt stresses. WRKY transcription factors are related to abiotic stress tolerance. The expression of the cowpea WRKY gene family in response to water deficit is not well known.
The genotypic drought response ranking is XiNong 9943 > XiNong 9940 > QianKu-5 > QianKu-4. XiNong 9943 shows drought tolerance and is useful for buckwheat breeding.

This was attributed to higher proline contents and antioxidant enzyme activity, and lower ROS accumulation and MDA content in transgenic lines compared to controls.

163 polymorphic loci were found in genome-wide screening. SNP-index values were 0.75 for the salt-tolerant offspring pool and 0.25 for the non-salt-tolerant offspring pool. 20 candidate genes were screened based on ANNOVAR annotation.

Genome-wide association studies of root-related traits were conducted using Automated Root Image Analysis (ARIA). 9,000 digital images were collected at three-time points: days 12, 15, and 18 after germination. Broad sense heritability for days 15 (0.22-0.73) and 18 (0.23-0.87) was higher than for day 12 (0.24-0.51).

QTL analysis of nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) in barley was conducted using AFLP markers and 94 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) from the Prisma x Apex mapping population. In total, 41 QTLs were detected on 6 chromosomes for 18 traits.
Three QTLs for barley GOA were mapped on chromosomes 2H and 7H. The major QTL QGOA-2H-2 was mapped on chromosome 2H, flanked by markers KDH and GBM1498, and explained 63.92% of phenotypic variation.

A winter wheat-summer foxtail millet-winter wheat rotation is typical, so early maturity of foxtail millet is critical. The objective was to develop a summer foxtail millet cultivar with early maturity and promising agronomical performance. 'Canggu 5' (Reg.

In phospholipid metabolism, phospholipase D genes were down-regulated and inositol and ethanolamine contents increased in Zhonggu2. Glycine and serine relative contents increased, and the serine hydroxymethyltransferase gene in glycine-serine metabolism was upregulated.

Common buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) is a staple food crop in southwest China. Drought stress is a major limiting factor that decreases crop production. To reveal the molecular mechanism of common buckwheat in response to drought stress, we performed a transcriptomics study to evaluate gene expression profiles during PEG-mediated drought treatment.

Association mapping was done to understand drought and heat tolerance genetic basis in chickpea. Phenotypic data for drought tolerance root traits, heat tolerance, yield and yield component traits were generated on a reference set (300 accessions, including 211 mini-core collection) from multiple seasons and locations in India and Africa.

Si treatment altered key metabolic pathways in oat leaves, including tryptophan metabolism, glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism, porphyrin metabolism, and chlorophyll metabolism. This provides insights into Si-mediated enhancement of oat resistance to stem rust.

Using a linkage map with 367 markers (DArT and SSRs) and an in vitro assay for germination stimulant activity towards Striga asiatica in 354 recombinant inbred lines from SRN39 (low stimulant) x Shanqui Red (high stimulant), the lgs gene was mapped on SBI-05 between microsatellite markers SB3344 and SB3352 at distances of 0.5 and 1.5 cM, respectively. The fine-mapped lgs region was delimited to a 5.8 cM interval with markers SB3344, SB3346 and SB3343 at 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 cM, respectively.

101 oat genotypes were evaluated. The genotypes comprised 51 cultivars and 50 breeding lines from eight Canadian oat breeding programs. They were evaluated for seedling reactions to six common Pca races and to a bulk Pca inoculum in greenhouse trials. They were also evaluated for adult plant resistance (APR) to natural Pca populations in field trials in 2014 and 2015. 66 genotypes showed resistance to at least one race. 22 of these were resistant to all six races.

Five ontologies (Gene Ontology, Trait Ontology, Plant Ontology, Growth Ontology, Environment Ontology) integrated drought information. Target genes linked to QTLs controlling yield and stress tolerance in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) and related species were identified.
Under drought stress, the auxin, cytokinin, and brassinosteroid signaling pathways were suppressed in Longyan 3. The abscisic acid and jasmonic acid signaling pathways were activated in DA92-2F6.

Drought stress exacerbated cell membrane damage, reduced chlorophyll content, and impaired antioxidant enzyme activity in both buckwheat varieties DK19 and K33. DK19 exhibited greater drought resistance than K33.

Hull color (HC) is a major indicator of nutritional quality in foxtail millet. To identify the gene or QTL for HC, RAD-seq analysis was used to reveal genome-wide SNPs and genotype the F-2 progeny from a cross between cultivar Heizhigu with green HC and cultivar Changnong 35 with yellow HC.

Genome-wide association mapping identified 39 significant marker-trait associations (MTAs) for pods/plant, seeds/pod, seed weight, and yield/plant. These include 15 major, 15 stable, and 13 both major and stable MTAs. Among the 39 MTAs, 29 are new, while 10 validate earlier studies. Seven markers are associated with multiple traits.

Pc45 was studied in the crosses 'AC Morgan'/Pc45 and 'Kasztan'/Pc45. F-2 progenies and F-2:3 families of both populations were inoculated with crown rust isolate CR258 (race NTGG). Single gene segregation ratios were observed.

Drought stress affects quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) production. The drought-tolerant quinoa genotype Dianli 129 was screened. Its seedling leaves were studied after drought and rewatering treatments using transcriptomics and targeted metabolomics.

Sorghum exhibits enhanced water uptake and reduced dissipation in arid environments to withstand drought stress. Sorghum exhibits drought resistance by adjusting osmotic potential, scavenging reactive oxygen species, and changing antioxidant enzyme activities.
Two models, RTM-GWAS and MLM-GWAS, were used to dissect the genetic architecture of agronomic traits based on 13,723 SNPs. Eleven QTLs for seven traits were identified using the two models.

The panicle length and weight decreased, and the empty abortive rate increased, resulting in yield reductions of 14.9% and 36.9%. Photosynthesis in millet significantly decreased, including net photosynthesis rate, stomatal conductance, and transpiration rate, especially under HD treatment with slow recovery after rehydration.

Path-coefficient analysis revealed that grains number on branches was the most dominant component of seed-setting rate, followed by grains number on stem. Grains number on branches had the greatest positive direct effect on seed-setting rate.

A high-density genetic map was constructed using a recombinant inbred line population between sorghum Tx623A and sudangrass Sa with RAD-seq. QTL mapping was performed for plant height (PH), stem diameter (SD), tiller number (TN), total shoot fresh weight (FW) and total shoot dry weight (DW). The map has 1,065 markers and a total length of 1191.7 cM.

The gene expression of SiHKTs under salt stress showed significant differences in different tissues. At the early stage of salt stress, SiHKTs transfer K+ into aboveground. Under salt stress, SiHKTs prevent sodium toxicity in root.

A novel wheat-rye derivative line LCR4 was developed through hybridization between hexaploid triticale line Currency and common wheat cultivar Jimai 22 (JM22). LCR4 was confirmed as a T2DS2DL-2RL translocation line via genomic in situ hybridization, multi-color fluorescence in situ hybridization, molecular marker analysis, and wheat SNP-arrays genotyping.

All SbCIPKs contain a conserved SNF1-like kinase domain in the N terminus and a NAF motif in the C terminus. Stress- and light-responsive cis-elements are present in the promoter regions of sorghum CIPKs.

Significant QTLs for SDW were mapped on LG10 with 15.5% PVE under well-watered conditions. A putative QTL for SDW was mapped on LG10 with 10.10% PVE under drought-stressed conditions in the F-3 population. Significant QTLs for NS, NDP, SW, and PW were mapped on LG4 (nearest markers: 4181663 and 4175954) with overlapping intervals and explained 21.9%, 21.8%, 23.5%, and 19.9% PVE respectively under well-watered conditions in the F-4 population. These are major QTLs controlling these traits.
Salicylic acid treatment reduced membrane permeability and Na+ content under salt stress. Yajin 13 had lower Na+ content and greater salinity tolerance than Yajin 71.
Ten breeder's MQTLs were selected from 25 validated MQTLs. Synteny analysis revealed orthologous relationships between eight breeder's MQTLs and 45 wheat MQTLs.

The highest predictive ability for DM was 0.34 using 137,191 SNPs. For HD it was 0.77 using 185,297 SNPs. For RUST it was 0.55 using 188,832 SNPs. Genomic prediction can optimize tetraploid ryegrass breeding.

Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) is a cereal crop. Its yield is limited by cold stress. We identified a novel gene, SiCST1 (Cold Stress Tolerance in Setaria italica 1), in foxtail millet through RNA-Seq of cold-stressed seedlings.

Transactivation analysis showed that SbSNAC1's transactivation activity is in the C-terminal region, with no activity in the conserved NAC-domain at the N-terminus. Subcellular localization assays using SbSNAC1 fragments fused with green fluorescent protein revealed that SbSNAC1 localizes in the nucleus, with the nuclear localization signal in the N-terminal section.
Tartary buckwheat is an abiotic resistant coarse cereal, but its stress tolerance mechanisms are largely unknown. MYB transcription factors regulate plant stress tolerance.

A high-density genetic linkage map was developed from a population of 172 F-2:12 recombinant inbred lines (RILs). The RILs were derived from a cross between the barley variety Yongjiabaidamai (YJ) and Hua 30 (H30). The map was used to map QTLs for spike length (SL), rachis node number (SRN), and spike density (SD). A total of 50 additive QTLs (LOD > 3) were mapped in four environments. Four of these QTLs were stable and major.
GWAS identified 24 SNPs significantly associated with traits. They include three SNPs with HT, four with TN, four with PL, three with Brix, and ten with RS.
BC3F3 families had genetic variation for selecting malting quality and agronomic traits. Ten breeding lines with improved beta-amylase thermostability also had improved yields and grain plumpness.

Different oat cultivars and treatment periods showed significant differences in gene expression after drought and salt stress treatments. Genes AsTCP021, AsTCP033, AsTCP044, AsTCP053, and AsTCP058 showed significant expression changes under both treatments. AsTCP053 was significantly upregulated at 24 h of stress treatment and showed a more sensitive response to salt stress.
The rice Erect Panicle2 (EP2) ortholog is a candidate gene in Pm 2-2. EP2 regulates panicle erectness and panicle length in rice.

F. esculentum and F. tataricum differ in water stress resistance. Water stress decreased leaf production, leaf fresh weight, leaf dry weight, stomatal conductance, transpiration rate, and photosynthesis rate in F. esculentum, but not in F. tataricum.
FtMYB10 from Tartary buckwheat was induced by ABA and drought. Transgenic lines were less sensitive to ABA in a germination test.

215 candidate genes were identified at these loci, including transcription factors, protein kinases, and other drought-responsive protein coding genes. Superior alleles associated with drought tolerance were identified and positively selected during breeding.

DEGs and DEMs participate in starch and sucrose metabolism and flavonoid biosynthesis. These processes improve drought tolerance in quinoa. Drought tolerance in quinoa correlates with gene expression differences, metabolite accumulation, and recovery after rewatering.

Reduction in N, P, K, Ca and Mg was found in all cultivars/lines, while Fe remained unchanged. Cultivars/lines NM-2006 and 8005 are drought tolerant. Cultivars/lines 97,006 and 97,001 are drought sensitive.

Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses compared two cultivars, elite variety Jingu 21 (JG21) and traditional landrace Niumaobai (NMB), during two grain-filling stages. 552 metabolites were identified, with 144 differentially abundant.

An F-6 RIL population from the cross Yugu 5 x Jigu 31 was phenotyped for leaf blast reactions in six field trials. An ultra-density genetic linkage map was constructed using 35,065 SNP markers from sequencing the RIL population.

A cross between Aininghuang and Jingu 21 produced an F-2 population of 543 foxtail millet plants. A high-density linkage map was constructed using RAD-seq. QTLs for 11 agronomic traits (PH, PL, PD, PNL, FID, SID, PW, GW, TGW, PT, PC) were mapped based on this map.

Resistance loci against pathotypes from Texas and Puerto Rico are flanked by SSR markers Ch5-55.0 and Ch5-56.1. The resistance locus against pathotypes from Arkansas is 9.5 cM below SSR marker Ch5-56.1. The resistance locus against pathotypes from Georgia is not in the distal region of chromosome 5.

text: Meta-QTLs on CaLG01 and CaLG06 harbor QTLs for traits including days to 50% flowering, days to maturity, days to flower initiation, days to pod initiation, number of filled pods, visual score, seed yield per plant, biological yield per plant, chlorophyll content, and harvest index. Key genes in Meta-QTL regions include Pollen receptor-like kinase 3 (CaPRK3), Flowering-promoting factor 1 (CaFPF1), Flowering Locus C (CaFLC), Heat stress transcription factor A-5 (CaHsfsA5), and Pollen-specific leucine-rich repeat extensins (CaLRXs). These genes regulate flowering time, pollen germination, and growth.
17 genes were abundantly expressed in Martin and HS41-1 compared with Moroc9-75 under both drought and control conditions. These genes were constitutively expressed in drought-tolerant genotypes.
Color was correlated with all compounds. Color QTL co-localized with carotenoid QTL. For beta-carotene, five QTL were on chromosomes 1, 2, and 10.

QTL alleles for increased height, later flowering and greater total dry matter yield were located on SBI-01 of R9403463-2-1 and SBI-06 of R9188. QTL alleles for increased grain yield from both R9403463-2-1 and R9188 were found on SBI-03.

Further analysis revealed ten predicted genes in this region. Four genes encode NBS-LRR proteins, indicating NBS-LRR genes are candidates for greenbug resistance. Genomic comparison of the SgR1 region suggested the four predicted NBS-LRRs are sorghum-specific and occurred after sorghum and maize divergence.

Mung bean (Vigna radiata) was subjected to a gradient of salt stress concentrations. Physiological assays and transcriptomic profiling were used. A dose-adapted time-ordered gene co-expression network (TO-GCN) analysis was performed to dissect the regulatory responses.
Proso millet is resilient to abiotic stress and drought. Its roots adapt and tolerate salt stress.

Secondary screening identified six genes with significant expression differences in the QTL region. These drought-responsive genes in foxtail millet are protein kinases, glycosyltransferases, CTP synthetases, and transcription factors.

27 loci on six barley chromosomes had resistance effects to at least one of five isolates. Almost all previously reported chromosomal regions for powdery mildew resistance genes were detected, plus a possible additional locus on chromosome 7.

A recombinant inbred line (RIL) population of 305 lines was derived from JG21 (high-carotenoid) and JG25 (low-carotenoid). The RIL population showed continuous phenotypic variation and significant transgressive segregation for carotenoid components (lutein, zeaxanthin, beta-cryptoxanthin) and kernel color, with zeaxanthin surpassing the higher parent.

The genes encoding glutathione S-transferase (GST), peroxidase (POD), phosphate transporter (PT), glucan endonuclease (GLU), beta-galactosidase (BGAL), cellulose synthase (CES), trichome birefringence-like protein (TBL), glycine-rich cell wall structural protein (GRP), glucosyltransferase (GT), GDSL esterase/lipase (GELP), cytochrome P450 (CYP), and jasmonate-induced protein (JIP) were differentially expressed. These genes may mediate osmotic adjustment, cell wall organization, reactive oxygen species scavenging, and plant hormone signaling to regulate responses to ethylene and salt stress.

Two ABA-responsive elements, ABRE1 (ACGTGTC) and ABRE2 (ACGTGGC), exist in the promoter of SiARDP. SiAREB1 and SiAREB2, two AREB-type transcription factors, bind to the ABRE core element in vitro and in vivo.

These loci were also detectable from the second last leaf of fully grown plants or the third leaves of seedlings, though with reduced efficiency. Using the high-quality genome assemblies of both parents of the mapping population, three candidate genes underlying the 6H QTL were predicted based on orthologous analysis.

A novel allele sdw1.ZU9 contains a 96-bp fragment in the promoter region of HvGA20ox2. This fragment is associated with lower gene expression, leading to lower plant height but higher germination rate. It was primarily observed in East Asian and Russian barley varieties.
Light and hormone responsive cis-acting elements were found in SiTPSs and SiTPPs. Low-temperature response elements were identified in SiTPS3, SiTPS4, SiTPS6, SiTPS7, SiTPS8, SiTPP4, and SiTPP5.

A field study tested the integrated effects of two planting densities (67,500 and 90,000 plants ha⁻¹) and three N rates (0, 180, and 360 kg ha⁻¹) on maize production. The higher planting density increased grain yield (GY), N use efficiency (NUE), agronomic N efficiency (AEN), and N partial productivity (PFP_N). It also decreased N₂O emission and greenhouse gas intensity.
29 putative HAK/KUP/KT proteins were identified from the Setaria italica genome database. These genes were distributed in seven chromosomes of foxtail millet.
Two millet cultivars, drought-resistant Yugu1 (YG) and drought-sensitive An04 (An), were used. Water use efficiency increased by 18.4% in An and 63.2% in YG under drought stress.

Except for the QTLs for plant height and NUE based on grain yield, no QTLs detected for a trait in 2005 expressed themselves in 2008 across nitrogen levels. QTLs controlling some traits were co-located each year. QTLs for many traits were detected on the same chromosome near the denso locus.
SbMYBHv33 negatively regulates salt tolerance and biomass accumulation in sorghum. It is an important component for sorghum growth, development, and salt stress response regulation.
Base editing targeted the SiALS and SiACC genes of foxtail millet using CBE and ABE. CBE targeting SiALS created a homozygous herbicide-tolerant mutant plant.

Carbon fixation in photosynthetic organisms and plant hormone signal transduction were enriched under drought stress. Expression levels of genes related to stress response and carbon metabolism were altered under drought stress.

Histochemical staining, interaction studies, and differential expression profiling suggest CaHSFA5 interacts with ROS scavenging genes to regulate ROS homeostasis for heat stress tolerance in chickpea. Heterologous expression and heat stress screening validated CaHSFA5's function in heat stress tolerance.

Lipidome and transcriptome analyses were applied to analyze the responses of membrane lipids to drought stress in two sorghum cultivars: drought-sensitive cv. Hongyingzi and drought-tolerant cv. Kangsi.
The morphological marker Trit is associated with a major QTL for resistance component traits. The QTL correspond to QTL or genes for insect resistance in syntenic maize genomic regions.
Gene-phenotype association analysis detected 113 genes associated with flowering time in barley. Two-way epistasis analysis revealed 19 pairs of gene-gene interactions controlling flowering time.

Transcriptome analysis identified 661 LN-responsive differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Among them, 17 genes are related to N transport and assimilation, and 29 genes are involved in hormone biosynthesis and signaling. These genes may play a role in Tartary buckwheat root development under LN.
Two QTLs were identified for biomass crystallinity index. This trait is inversely correlated with conversion efficiency in bioenergy grasses.

2792 transcription factors and 1223 transcriptional regulators were identified. 318 TFs and 149 TRs were differentially expressed under heat stress. 315 TFs and 128 TRs were differentially expressed under drought stress.

The oat cultivar Baiyan 2 at the three-leaf stage was used to investigate drought resistance. Seedlings were treated with polyethylene glycol (PEG) to simulate drought stress. Photosynthetic parameters and physicochemical indices were measured at 6 h and 12 h and compared to the control at 0 h.

DEGs involved in ROS detoxification in HN16 worked through different means. Analysis of three DEGs encoding APX and GPX revealed that SbAPx1, SbGPx1, and SbGPx2 all played an important role in RMES1-mediated resistance to aphids.

A high-density genetic map was constructed for the cross Tx623A x S722 using 103 recombinant inbred lines (RILs). The map contains 1610 markers and spans 2329 cM. QTL mapping identified 19 QTLs: two for plant height (PH), three for stem diameter (SD), four for tiller number (TN), four for fresh weight (FW), and five for dry weight (DW).
Foxtail millet (Setaria italica L.) resists drought stress. Its drought stress resistance molecular mechanisms are unclear.
13 of 15 alleles were polymorphic. The SSR marker had an average PIC of 0.205.

A genetic linkage map was constructed using an F2 population from the cross between foxtail millet lines Changsheng07 and Donggu218. The map included 159 SSR markers and 37 Indel markers, covered 1545.5 cM, and had an average marker distance of 7.89 cM.

Based on a high-density variation map, we identified genome-level evidence for local adaptation. Siprr37 with transposon insertion contributes to the fitness of foxtail millet in the northeastern ecoregion.

Narrow leaf width is correlated with greater intrinsic water use efficiency in C-4 species. This study evaluated the correlation of leaf width with whole-plant TE and investigated the genetic control of leaf width in sorghum.

Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) is threatened by rust disease caused by Uromyces setariae-italicae (Usi). The NAC transcription factor family is a plant-specific regulatory gene family involved in stress responses.

A novel QTL qRYM-7H/qTFRYM-7H for barley yellow mosaic resistance was identified by GWAS and linkage analysis. Candidate genes for qRYM-7H/qTFRYM-7H were predicted based on transcriptome sequencing and qPCR analysis.

The QTL on CHR 6H has the largest effect, explaining up to 20.9% of phenotypic variance. FLT interacts with flag leaf width and area, and correlates with fertile tiller number, spike row types, kernel number per spike, and heading date.

A chromosome-anchored genetic map was developed for an oat recombinant inbred population. SNP markers linked to QTL affecting root growth response to Al were identified. Three QTL on chromosomes 7C-17A, 13A, and 19A confer Al tolerance. They were identified using primary root regrowth of recombinant inbred lines from the cross between UFRGS 17 (Al tolerant) and UFRGS 930598-6 (Al sensitive).

Seedling resistance was evaluated as infection type (IT) using isolates of four pathogen races (DBD, SGD, TGN, and TJS). Seventeen QTL were detected, including ten at the adult plant stage, five at the seedling stage, and two shared across stages.

An integrated genomic strategy delineates a gene and alleles for a major QTL governing heat stress tolerance in chickpea. This can accelerate marker-assisted breeding and gene editing to develop high-yielding heat stress tolerant chickpea varieties.

GO and KEGG pathway analysis identified DEGs enriched in photosynthesis, chlorophyll metabolism, amino acid metabolism, and carbohydrate metabolism in three cultivars. 46 genes had transcription change trends consistent with drought resistance trends among three foxtail millet cultivars.

Four Sorghum bicolor genotypes were screened in a dry-down experiment. Different drought response strategies were identified among the four genotypes and the two Sorghum races. The durra race is more drought tolerant than the caudatum race. Within the durra race, genotype IS22330 is drought tolerant.

A GWAS used 87 barley landraces (39 hulled, 48 hulless) with 191,098 SNP markers. The population had four sub-populations (POP1 to POP4). Beta-glucan content in POP2 was significantly higher than in other groups. Most hulless barley landraces in POP2 are from the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau in China.

The study identified 54 bZIP proteins in V. radiata and 50 in V. angularis. It surveyed bZIP gene characteristics, including structure, chromosome distribution, and motif composition. Phylogenetic analysis divided VrbZIP and VabZIP proteins into ten clades.

SSR marker CEDG304 on LG9 of yardlong bean associated with resistance. ICIM identified a major QTL, qCLS9.1, for resistance on LG9. qCLS9.1 accounted for 25.40-89.26% of disease score variation. qCLS9.1 is likely the same as QTL ALS10.1 conferring resistance to angular leaf spot disease in common bean.

Different Zn application methods increased total polyphenol, carotenoid, total flavonoid, and Zn contents in foxtail millet grains. Under basal soil application (S3) and foliar spray (F2), total flavonoid content increased by 45.87% and 64.40% compared to CK.

High ammonium toxicity severely affects plant growth and crop production. Breeding high NH4+-tolerant and high-yield plants is urgent. The molecular mechanisms of plant response and tolerance to high NH4+ are poorly understood.
Seven CAMTA genes were identified in the quinoa genome. The expression patterns of CqCAMTAs were analyzed in root and leaf tissues.

Drought-tolerance mechanisms during the jointing stage in foxtail millet under water-limited conditions were characterized. Two drought-tolerant and two drought-sensitive cultivars were examined using transcriptomic dissections of root, stem, and leaf tissues.

Two candidate genes, HORVU7Hr1G000320 and HORVU7Hr1G000040, are linked to SNP7. They belong to the nucleotide triphosphate hydrolase superfamily and may affect beta-glucan synthase activity. Another candidate gene, HORVU1Hr1G000010, is associated with SNP1 and may be involved in sugar response.

A major QTL (qPJ6.1) on chromosome 6 is associated with the plant juice trait (PJ) and explains 35.2% of its phenotypic variation. For fresh biomass weight (FBW), four major QTLs (qFBW1.1, qFBW6.1, qFBW7.1, and qFBW9.1) are located on chromosomes 1, 6, 7, and 9, explaining 12.3%, 14.5%, 10.6%, and 11.9% of the phenotypic variation, respectively.
Mungbean is an important food legume crop adapted to drought environments, but severe drought curtails its production. We resequenced 282 mungbean accessions to identify genome-wide variants.

Naked oat is grown in marginal environments where drought stress limits yield. In a field and rainout shelter study, six genotypes were compared for yield, water relations, and physiological and biochemical responses to drought. Three genotypes were recently released (RR) since 2008, and three were early-released (ER) at least 60 years earlier.

The CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout mutant of the rice homolog of SiCST1, designated oscst1, exhibited cold sensitivity. Compared to wild-type rice, oscst1 mutant seedlings had a 46% reduction in survival rate under cold stress.

Grain yield of Sorghum bicolor is influenced by variation in traits including tiller number, plant height, and time of anthesis. In a population of 137 recombinant inbred lines, at least 27 QTLs controlling nine morphological traits were mapped. The percentage of additive genetic variance explained by the QTLs was determined.
Qing1 increased by 33.56%, 38.95%, and 25.06%. Long4 increased by 29.01%, 40.05%, and 22.35%. Their MDA content was 20.6% and 9.41% lower than the control.

19 small secreted peptides (SSPs) encoding genes, including FtCLE7 and FtCEP3, respond to high NH4+. The up-regulation of FtCLE7 and down-regulation of FtCEP3 may help plants optimize root response to high NH4+.

Five new markers were developed for marker-assisted selection. QTLs including qPC7-2 for PC, qPW5-1 for PW and qPH5-2 for PH were verified via correlation analysis of markers to traits in the natural population and the advanced generation population AJF(5) derived from the mapping population by single seed descent.
Sorghum is adaptable to drought and high temperature. Group 3 LEA genes from barley and rice play a crucial role in abiotic stress tolerance.

Transcriptome sequencing was performed on sorghum seedling leaves before and after cold treatment. Candidate genes for cold tolerance and regulation pathways for photosynthesis under cold stress were identified.

Correlation analysis between transcriptomics and proteomics identified four types of differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in the JIA2 differential gene-protein interaction network under severe stress. These included 13 key DEGs and DEPs related to plant hormone signal transduction, secondary metabolite biosynthesis, carbohydrate metabolism, and metabolic pathways.

A total of 2155 and 3033 candidate genes involved in domestication, and 84 and 180 candidate genes related to improvement, were identified at the seedling and filling stages of broomcorn millet, respectively. Genes related to metabolites, stress resistance, and plant hormones were widely selected during domestication and improvement. Some genes were exclusively selected in either domestication or improvement stages. Higher selection pressure was detected in the domestication process.
12 SbPUB genes contain MYB-related elements, which are regulators of flavonoid biosynthesis. These results are consistent with a previous multi-omics analysis of sorghum under salt stress.

Genetic improvements in feedstock quality, including biomass total yield and conversion efficiency, are needed for lignocellulosic bioenergy. Studies have identified candidate genes and QTL associated with total biomass accumulation and grain production in maize and sorghum.

Chlorophyll fluorescence parameters were not affected by water stress in either species. Chlorophyll content increased in water-stressed plants in both species. Oxidative stress occurred in both species under water stress. Antioxidant content increased in F. tataricum.

Heterologous expression of SbCASP4 increased salt stress tolerance in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana. Under 50 mM NaCl treatment, SbCASP4-expression lines had less leaf Na+, lower PI accumulation in stele, smaller oxidative damage, higher salinity threshold, longer root length, and higher expression of Casparian strip formation genes compared to wild type and casp5 mutants.
Five QTL-regions were validated. They showed consistent effect in the GWAS population and the breeding material.

The phenotype of 126 RILs and their parents Tx623A (sorghum) and Sa (Sudangrass) was characterized for two years. The phenotypes included five forage quality traits: crude protein (CP), neutral detergent fiber (NDF), acid detergent fiber (ADF), acid detergent lignin (ADL), and hemicellulose (HC) content. 19 QTLs controlling these traits were mapped in the RIL population between sorghum Tx623A and sudangrass Sa.

High-yielding varieties had 12-13.7% higher stem base hardness and 6.3-11.5% higher middle stem hardness than medium- and low-yield varieties. They also showed increased dry matter accumulation, decreased effective branch number, increased main ear length, and increased 1000-grain weight.
SiLRR-RLK genes are unevenly distributed across chromosomes. Several SiLRR-RLK family members are involved in stress response pathways under biotic and abiotic stress conditions.

Greater relative green leaf area during late grain filling was related to greater relative grain yield in two post-flowering moisture deficit environments (r² = 0.34 in 2004-2005 and r² = 0.76 in 2005-2006). Leaf chlorophyll was also related to yield in one post-flowering stress environment (r² = 0.42, P < 0.05). The marker-assisted backcross transfer of stay-green QTLs from B35 into an adapted but senescent background can enhance tolerance of post-flowering drought stress in sorghum.

Five stable QTLs are co-located on chromosome 3H flanked by markers bpb6282426 and bpb4786261. They are Qgna.sau-3H for grain N concentration, Qtna.sau-3H for total N accumulation per plant, Qnhi.sau-3H for N harvest index, Qnutegy.sau-3H for N utilization efficiency for grain yield, and Qanutedm.sau-3H.1 for N utilization efficiency for aboveground dry matter. These QTL clusters control NUE traits at seedling and maturity stages.
